newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: South Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand ended steady on Tuesday after strong demand for dollars from offshore and from local importers was met by Reserve Bank dollar sales, forex dealers said.
It closed at 4.6840/6890 on the dollar, unchanged from Monday's levels after briefly testing 4.69 during the day on the back of London dollar buying.
"The central bank was steadfast at the top, keeping the rand from weakening above 4.69," a forex trader at a foreign bank said.
He said there had been strong demand for dollars from London, local importers and via the options market which was met by central bank (dollar) sales.
"The overall bias is towards more weakness and there is a chance that we could move above 4.70 over the next few days," the dealer added.
Other traders said the rand tested a 4.6920 high bid shortly before noon amid good two-way dealings.
"London buyers pushed the rand weaker to above the 4.69 level where it was met by offers," a trader at one of the major big four banks said.
He said morning trade was characterised by good two-way dealings on both sides of a 4.6880 to 4.6910 range.

A dearth of fresh news had stifled direction although the market had initially reacted slightly negatively to reports that state telecommunications utility Telkom was expected to announce a sharp increase in local telephone tariffs on Wednesday as part of a move to eliminate local call rate subsidisation.
Against the crosses, the rand was last quoted at 7.7235/7364 against sterling from 7.7099/7204 previously and at 0.3310/3314 marks from 0.3314/3319 marks.
It was a listless day on the South African bond market as players took to the sidelines and activity started to wind down ahead of the festive season.
But bond traders cautioned that it was premature to talk of a quiet December month.
The benchmark R150 stock was last quoted at 15.93 percent from 15.94 percent late on Monday after hovering around 15.945 percent during the morning session.
"It was exceptionally quiet...there were no positions in the market," a bond trader said.
He expected a 16.00 percent to 15.80 percent range in the near-term with both levels providing strong resistance on the upside and downside respectively.
Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners were net buyers of local bonds to the tune of 97.12 million rand on Monday after buying 19.05 million rand on Friday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 4.99 billion rand on Monday from 4.72 billion rand on Friday.

On the money market, three-month NCD rates were quoted slightly higher at between 17.20 to 17.25 percent offered from 17.15 and 17.20 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate also moved slightly higher to be quoted in a 16.55 and 16.80 percent range from a 16.50 to 16.75 percent range.
The Reserve Bank indicated the money market shortage higher at 9.340 billion rand on Monday from 8.761 billion rand on Saturday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
